**Risk officer assessment: REFUSE.**

The brief is internally contradictory and the data points to a manipulated launch. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0, only 5 curve buyers, and a completer_share of 0.94, meaning nearly all the curve was filled by a bundle, not organic demand. Yet the class is labeled ORGANIC, and the first two minutes show 91 buyers. Those two claims can't both be true, and I'd trust the curve data. The 548-buyer last-15-minute figure with a 0.49 return looks like wash or bot activity layered on a bundled launch.

The launch bot present, a sell/buy ratio of 0.72 right after graduation, and a 0.49 return in 15 minutes all raise the risk of a dump on any dip. The pool depth of 165 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket, but depth doesn't offset a bundled supply.

No size, stop, or hold time is sane here. Skip.
memos.scout:
Case for buying: the last 15 minutes show real two-sided activity: 548 buyers and 193 sellers, 456 SOL bought against 417 sold, and a 49% return over that window. The coin is 31 minutes old, still alive, and only 6.5% off its 30-minute high, so it has not broken down. Pool depth of 165 SOL is reasonable for a $20 ticket, keeping price impact modest. The 2-minute post-graduation flow looks broad rather than concentrated: 91 external buyers, and the top 5 buyers hold only 35% of that volume.

Case against, which I think dominates: the curve is 100% bundle-share with 5 buyers and 94% completer share, a bundled launch pattern. Top 3 hold 86% of the curve, and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes was 0.72 with a launch bot present. The organic-looking late flow may simply be the same wallets distributing into retail demand. A 49% run from a bundled launch is the classic setup for a 30-60 minute fade, and the base rate for random buys in this window is roughly -20% per trade before fees of 1.4-5.1%.

Verdict: the demand signal is real on the surface, but the bundling and concentrated curve make it unlikely to persist. I would skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is insider distribution after a pump. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0 with buyers at only 5 and completer_share 0.9356, meaning nearly all the curve was filled by a bundled group, with top3 holding 86%. The first two minutes after graduation show 184.71 SOL bought against a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.72 and a launch bot present, which suggests early holders are already exiting. The last 15 minutes show 416.85 SOL sold versus 456.36 bought, and net flow has been positive only because of a late retail wave (548 buyers, 193 sellers). The +49% return and 6.5% drawdown from the 30-minute high are typical of a coin near its exit. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a shallow 165 SOL pool, a modest dip erases any edge. Pass.
